author: ohtadmin
title: BACK TO SCHOOL
text:
The principals of the two local schools are looking forward to a “bustling” first day when students return to the classroom next week.
The 2025-26 academic year at Melrose and Lawn schools will commence Tuesday, Sept. 2.
“It always has such a positive energy when the kids and teachers come back,” said Beth Roman, principal of the elementary school on Melrose Avenue.
Lawn principal Nate Edmunds echoed Roman’s thoughts following a quiet summer at the middle school.
“I’m most interested in that,” he said. “I can’t wait to just have everybody back. I enjoy it when we’re all here together.”
Edmunds’ students in grades 5-8 will gather in the courtyard for an introductory assembly that will include a “step to the line” game. He said the event helps introduce new staff and students to the district by being “outside all together.”
“I like to give the kids a little bit of time to visit with each other,” Edmunds said. “There’s a lot of excitement on that first day.”
New Lawn curriculum
This year, new social studies standards from the Rhode Island Department of Education will be introduced into Lawn classrooms. The standards were approved in 2023 and feature different topics for every grade from kindergarten through high school.
Fifth-graders will learn about American history through the Reconstruction period following the Civil War, for example, and eighth-graders will study government and civics. Edmunds called it a “readjustment of what is taught when.”
“They’ve moved certain time periods to different grade levels,” he said.
The school has aligned other subjects to these standards. For instance, sixth-grade students will be reading “The Lightning Thief,” the first novel in the Percy Jackson series by Rick Riordan, in their English class. That book series is themed around Greek mythology and the topic of Greek gods will be simultaneously taught in their social studies classes.
The science classes have been transitioning to a program called OpenSciEd. A fifth-grade unit was piloted in 2023-24 and that will continue this year. The middle school also is continuing its focus on writing in its classrooms across all subjects.
The school is changing its setup for their “Genius Hour,” which is a segment of the week in which seventh- and eighth-grade students investigate a topic of their interest during the “ROCK Block” segment of the day. This year, the two grades will spend a quarter of the year on their “Genius Hour” topics, with the eighth-graders working in their first quarter and the seventh-graders in the final quarter.
“We’re devoting more time to that, and really helping the student organize and go deep,” Edmunds said. “The Genius Hour has been very cool. It’s akin to a senior project.”
Lawn School is also expanding its interest-based advisory program, which previously was just once a year. That program will now be available in the fall and spring due to the popularity with both students and faculty. In the program, teachers host workshops on non-scholastic subjects, such as gardening and needlepoint.
“Whatever a teacher might have a strength in, or an interest in, we’re able to offer more choices to kids,” Edmunds said. “The kids really respond very well to it. They like to learn something new.”
In addition to the returning students, the schools also have welcomed families that are new to Jamestown. An ice cream social was hosted for those families Tuesday at Melrose School. It gave these families the opportunity to meet community groups, such as the Boy Scouts, Conanicut Island Sailing Foundation and Jamestown Community Theatre. Some of those new students are from families of military personnel studying at the U.S. Naval Station Newport, and only will be staying in Jamestown a year or two.
Edmunds extended his gratitude to Amanda Bridges, a seventh-grade math teacher who organizes the annual social.
“It’s not just an ice cream social,” he said. “She has organized all these wonderful community partners to come and introduce themselves to the new families of Jamestown. It’s a great way to get new interest in some of the community groups that are out there. It’s just a wonderful afternoon.”
Melrose shuffles teachers
At Melrose School, there is an orientation Thursday, Aug. 28, for pre-kindergarten and kindergarten students. New families are welcome to tour the school following the event.
Roman said her staff at the elementary school tend to keep things calm on the first day. The students will start their day on the playground and the teachers will meet their classes there.
“They start the day in their own spaces,” Roman said. “Really celebrating their community, seeing the new students that are in their new community, seeing their new classrooms, starting to get their desks and their cubbies settled.”
This year, there will be a third classroom for both kindergarten and fourth grade due to the sizes of those two grades.
“The third grade that went into fourth grade has been high numbers for a while,” Roman said. “It’s kind of our bubble class.”
In addition to a new teacher and classroom, the fourth-grade wing was redesigned during the summer with new furniture and rugs as part of work covered under the capital budget. The third- and fourth-grade classrooms have new smartboards, and the school’s office space also was redesigned. Roman credits maintenance director Peter Anderson and his crew for their work during the summer.
“They’ve been hard at work trying to give this beautiful building a facelift,” Roman said. “We’re really excited about that.”
Melrose also has a new STEAM lab with new furniture to complement the curriculum, which encompasses science, technology, engineering, arts and mathematics curriculum. Roman said students this year will be learning hydroponics.
